about: A button-actuation benchmark entry (G13, train) in dev.json format, modelled on E1-01. Tier 4: a perfboard with a 2 x 2 button array and a socketed Pico 2 from the parts catalogue, a base and a lid (top plate) with a pattern of plunger holes, four printed plungers with a stated clearance, travel and actuation, a rear USB opening, standoffs, and a screw-closed lid, judged as interference and clearance checks against reference models and keep-out volumes. L1 ids match requirements.md next to this file (L2/L3 tree, reference models, assumptions, fixed decisions, feasibility, traceability). Numbers that are not in the plan brief come from requirements.md section 3. Never put any of these numbers in agent logic: they belong in the request text, requirements, design_rules.json generic values and part.json catalogue data.

methods.inspection: read from the design or mesh (counts, sizes, positions, relations)
methods.analysis: computed by Python (stability, connectivity, interference and clearance against reference models, hand calculations)
methods.demonstration: a stand-in object is placed in the design (fits, rests, does not slide)
methods.test: a probe is applied (insert a plug along its axis, drop the part in, sweep a tool, load path)

requests.title: Pico macro pad with four buttons
requests.request: A 2 x 2 macro pad. Four 6 mm tactile switches sit on a 70 x 50 mm perfboard (a mounting hole in each corner) at 19.05 mm pitch in both directions, with a Raspberry Pi Pico 2 plugged into female sockets on the same board behind them. Each switch is pressed by a printed plunger that comes up through a hole in the top plate with 0.4 mm clearance all round, and the plunger has 1.5 mm of travel before it bottoms out. The Pico's micro-USB port opens through the rear end wall, so the cable plugs in with the lid on. The enclosure is a base and a removable top plate (the plate is the lid), printed on an FDM printer without supports.
requests.request_notes: Added to the plan brief, all from requirements.md section 3: 'above them' = behind the buttons, further along +Y (A1); 'rear' = the short end wall the Pico's USB faces (A2); the Pico on female sockets (A3, the plan lists a female header); the plunger is a printed part with a stem, a retaining flange and a stop (A5); 0.4 mm clearance per side (A6); lid screws M3 into bosses outside the board (F2); FDM, no supports (A10).

l1.text: The design shall place the four tactile switches in a 2 x 2 array at 19.05 mm pitch and the Pico 2 on female sockets behind them on the 70 x 50 mm board, from the parts catalogue, with the Pico's USB port facing the rear short end, without the parts colliding or covering the corner holes, and shall declare that layout.
The 70 x 50 x 1.6 mm board shall fit inside the closed enclosure with at least 0.5 mm clearance to every printed surface, apart from where it rests on its standoffs.

The board shall rest on exactly four standoffs, one under each corner hole, each 5 to 7 mm in outside diameter, with its top plane within 0.1 mm of the others and a pilot hole for an M2 self-tapping screw through the board.

With the lid closed, no part of the base or the lid shall come within 13.3 mm above the board's top surface or 4 mm below its underside, except the standoffs under the holes, and the Pico, the sockets and the switches shall lie inside the enclosure.

With the lid closed, a micro-USB cable shall plug fully into the Pico through one opening in the rear end wall without touching the enclosure (at least 0.3 mm clear all round), and that opening shall be no more than 1.5 mm bigger than the plug on any side.

Each switch shall have its own printed plunger that comes up through a round hole in the top plate, coaxial with the switch (within 0.2 mm), with 0.4 mm clearance on every side between plunger and hole; each plunger has a round stem 4.0 to 5.6 mm in diameter and a tip face at least 3.5 mm across.

Each plunger shall have 1.5 mm of travel before it bottoms out, shall reach the switch's actuation point before bottoming without crushing the switch, shall stay proud of the plate by at least 0.5 mm at the end of its travel, and shall stay in the plate when the case is turned over, held by a flange at least 2 mm wider than the hole that rests against the underside of the plate.

The enclosure shall be a base and a separate removable lid, a flat plate that drops into a rebate in the top of the walls (plate 2 to 3 mm thick, 0.15 to 0.35 mm fit gap per side, upstand at least 1 mm) and is screwed down with four M3 self-tapping screws into four bosses in the base.
The closed enclosure shall have no openings other than the USB opening, the four plunger holes and screw holes, and its walls, floor and lid shall be 2 to 4 mm thick.
The base, the lid and the plunger shall each be one manifold body that prints on an FDM printer without supports (no overhang steeper than 45° from vertical, no bridge over 15 mm).
The closed enclosure shall be no larger than 95 x 70 x 35 mm, longest along the board's 70 mm side, and shall stand flat on a desk without tipping.

The plungers shall load into the lid from below, the populated board shall drop straight down onto its standoffs with the lid off, the lid with its plungers shall close over the board, and every screw shall be reachable with a screwdriver.

The design shall be delivered as a base STL, a lid STL, a plunger STL, the OpenSCAD source, the declared layout and the agent's own clearance report, and that report shall agree with an independent measurement.
